property_summary: After a player sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT and the pseudo-random outcome is a win (random==0), the pot must be fully paid out and reset to zero; the mutant tracks pot via the constant instead of msg.value, so any divergence in the recorded pot breaks this invariant.

For every accepted play (msg.value must equal TICKET_AMOUNT), the contract's recorded pot exactly equals the ETH it holds: after any successful call to play, address(c).balance == c.pot(); the mutant that credits the constant instead of the actual msg.value desynchronizes the recorded pot from the real balance whenever the credited amount diverges from what was actually paid in.

For every accepted play, the contract's recorded pot exactly accounts for all ETH it holds: after a winning round (random==0) the pot must be zero and the contract must retain exactly the 1-wei fee, and after a losing round the retained ETH must equal the pot; the mutant credits the constant instead of the actual received value, desynchronizing pot from the real balance.

For any admissible input, a winning play (random==0) by a funded player must reset the recorded pot to zero and leave the contract holding exactly the 1-wei fee, so the recorded pot always matches what was actually paid in; the mutant that credits a constant instead of msg.value desynchronizes the recorded pot from real contributions and breaks this rule.

For any accepted play (msg.value == TICKET_AMOUNT = 10 wei), the reference C keeps its recorded pot perfectly synchronized with the ETH it actually holds: after a winning round pot is reset to 0 and the contract retains exactly the 1-wei fee, while after a losing round the balance equals the pot; the mutant crediting the constant instead of msg.value desynchronizes pot from the real contributions, breaking this rule.

For any timestamp/difficulty pair making the pseudorandom value 0, a winning play must pay out and reset pot to 0; the mutant only pays out when the random value is 1, leaving pot nonzero in those cases.

For any admissible setup where the pseudorandom outcome equals 1, a winning-in-mutant play must NOT reset the pot (the reference leaves pot at 10), while the mutant resets pot to 0, breaking the invariant that pot is nonzero after a play whose random value is 1.
After any sequence of plays, the contract's ether balance always equals its accumulated pot (all deposits remain until paid out in full on a win).
